text:
Two goals in 21 seconds, late in a tied game, settled this one, and neither was the kind of chance that usually settles anything. Brandon Hagel's wrister at 18:16 of the third carried a 3 percent chance of scoring, and he followed it with a snap shot at 18:37 that was a coin flip at 49. That gave Tampa Bay a 5-3 win over the Islanders, even though the New York side that trailed 3-0 in the chances column through one period climbed back to a 3-3 tie by the end of the second.

By the numbers, this was close to a push. Tampa Bay finished with 3.06 expected goals to 2.51, but at even strength the Islanders held the edge, 1.45 to 1.26, and the simulated replays of every shot give the Lightning only a 51 percent claim on the win. The second period was New York's: 1.75 expected goals to 1.38, with Tony DeAngelo, Jean-Gabriel Pageau and Brayden Schenn all scoring. Schenn's tip-in on the power play with seven seconds left in the period was a 67 percent chance, the best look of the night, and it erased a 3-1 deficit. Matthew Schaefer logged 27 minutes and put eight shots on net.

Tampa Bay had the better third, 1.05 to 0.46, and Hagel finished with three goals and an assist on 1.27 individual expected goals, so he earned most of what he got. Jake Guentzel added two, including a power-play goal in the second. Ilya Sorokin allowed 4 goals on 2.56 expected, about one and a half more than the shots deserved, while Andrei Vasilevskiy was a half goal worse than expected himself. The Lightning's late burst was lucky in shape, but it came in the period they controlled.
